title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages. M is a free module of rank 2, and rho, sigma lie in GL(M). In 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' these are presumably the images of the standard generators in a rank-2 linear 'loop equation' problem. The hypothesis (40 bis) is that eps_1 = -lambda_0 rho sigma^{-1} is unipotent, i.e. eps_1 = 1 + N_1 with N_1^2 = 0. So rho sigma^{-1} is a scalar times a transvection.

One sets eps_0 = rho^{-1} eps_1 rho = 1 + N_0, with N_0 = -(lambda_0 sigma^{-1} rho + 1). This gives one-parameter additive subgroups L_i = {eps_i(lambda) = 1 + lambda N_i}. B_0 is the normalizer of L_0 in GL(M), carrying two characters:
- chi = det;
- chi', defined by u N_0 u^{-1} = chi'(u) N_0.
The subgroup B~_0 is defined by chi = chi'.

In a basis with N_0 = e_12, B_0 is the Borel subgroup, u = [[a,b],[0,d]], chi' = a/d and chi = ad. So B~_0 = {d^2 = 1}. The starred subgroup B~_0^* is presumably the component d = 1, i.e. u acts trivially on M/Im N_0. That is the affine group 'ax+b', and 1 -> L_0 -> B~_0^* --det--> G_m -> 1 is exact.

This page. For u a section of B~_0^*, put xi = [u,rho] and eta = [u,sigma] (commutators u g u^{-1} g^{-1}). Grothendieck wants to prove xi = eta * eps_1(mu - 1), with mu = det u (formula 64).

Sanity check for u = eps_0(lambda) in L_0:
- rho N_0 rho^{-1} = N_1 holds by definition.
- sigma N_0 sigma^{-1} = -(lambda_0 rho sigma^{-1} + 1) = N_1 follows from (57) and (49).
- Hence rho eps_0(lambda) rho^{-1} = sigma eps_0(lambda) sigma^{-1} = eps_1(lambda) (formula 65).
- So [u,rho] = [u,sigma] = eps_0(lambda) eps_1(-lambda), consistent with (64) since mu = 1.

The next page reduces the general case to int(eps_1)(v) = v * eps_1(1/mu - 1) for v in B~_1. This uses int(rho sigma^{-1}) = int(eps_1), since the two differ by a scalar. It is a one-line 2x2 check: with eps_1 = [[1,1],[0,1]] and v = [[a,b],[0,d]], d = ±1, both sides equal [[a, b + d - a],[0,d]] when t = 1/mu - 1.

Purpose: to parametrize the solutions of the 'loop equation' by the solvable group B~_0 (an affine-group torsor structure). This is a step in the rank-2 linear analysis of the equation.
errors: Sign slip under the brace: eps_0(-lambda) = 1 - lambda N_0, not 1 + N_0 lambda. Consequently sigma eps_0(-lambda) sigma^{-1} = eps_1(-lambda); the conclusion is unaffected.

Previous page: the exact sequence 1 -> L_0 -> B~_0 -> G_m -> 1 is false for B~_0 as defined, since the kernel of det is mu_2 x L_0 (d = ±1). This is presumably why the star B~_0^* (the component d = 1) appears here, and why the margin says 'il faudrait le vérifier'.
Identity (64) is only verified on this page for u in L_0. The general case is deferred to the next page, where it reduces to a trivial check that in fact holds on all of B~_1 (both components).

ideas.what: Rank-2 setup in which rho sigma^{-1} is a scalar times a transvection; conjugation by rho and sigma both carry the transvection group L_0 onto L_1
ideas.modern_name: pseudo-reflection (scalar times transvection) local monodromy in rank-2 representations of a free group on two generators, cf. hypergeometric monodromy
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche / Esquisse discuss related rank-2 and Teichmüller-tower questions, but not this computation as far as known

ideas.what: The subgroup B~_0 of the normalizer of a transvection group cut out by det = (character on N_0), giving an extension of G_m by G_a (affine group ax+b)
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup / affine group Aff_1 as a stabilizer

ideas.what: Commutator identity [u,rho] = [u,sigma] eps_1(det u - 1) for u in B~_0, equivalently int(eps_1)(v) = v eps_1(1/det v - 1)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine 2x2 matrix verification inside a longer rank-2 analysis of the 'loop equation'. It is correct up to a harmless sign slip; nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The underbrace under eps_0(-lambda) indeed reads '1+N_0 lambda' in the image, but it should mathematically be 1 - lambda N_0. The transcription is faithful; this is Grothendieck's slip.
Page number at top of image is '439' (Grothendieck's own numbering); archive page 275.
'or [-Kl-] {+cf.+} calculs de (57)': the crossed-out letters look like 'Kl' or 'Al'; the reading 'cf. calculs de (57)' is plausible.
